::: {.reference-list}
1. IRI. *Guide to PyCPT 2 for Seasonal Climate Forecasts* (Jupyter Book, 2 September 2023 build): The Climate Predictability Tool (CPT). <https://iri.columbia.edu/~awr/pycpt/seasonal-jupyterbook/html_2sep2023/cpt.html>
2. IRI. *CPT+: Climate Predictability Tool*. <https://iri.columbia.edu/our-expertise/climate/tools/cpt/>
3. IRI Data Library. *NMME NCEP-CFSv2 hindcasts, PENTAD_SAMPLES_FULL, precipitation*. <https://iridl.ldeo.columbia.edu/SOURCES/.Models/.NMME/.NCEP-CFSv2/.HINDCAST/.PENTAD_SAMPLES_FULL/.prec/> Browsing Data Library pages requires signing in (checked 10 November 2026); PyCPT's data requests in this tutorial succeeded without a key.
4. Saha, S., Moorthi, S., Wu, X., et al. (2014). The NCEP Climate Forecast System Version 2. *Journal of Climate*, 27(6), 2185-2208. <https://doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-12-00823.1>
5. Kirtman, B., Min, D., Infanti, J., et al. (2014). The North American Multimodel Ensemble: Phase-1 seasonal-to-interannual prediction; Phase-2 toward developing intraseasonal prediction. *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*, 95(4), 585-601. <https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-12-00050.1>
6. Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara. *CHIRPS: Rainfall Estimates from Rain Gauge and Satellite Observations* (CHIRPS version 3.0 page). <https://www.chc.ucsb.edu/data/chirps3>
7. Funk, C., Peterson, P., Landsfeld, M., et al. (2014). *A quasi-global precipitation time series for drought monitoring*. U.S. Geological Survey Data Series 832. <https://doi.org/10.3133/ds832>
:::
